raw_response:
I have 16.1 mu of land. I plant 10 mu of cotton and 6.1 mu of stevia. I am 68 years old and I have been doing this for 35 years. I only went to primary school, but I know my fields better than any book.

For cotton, I will till with the rotary machine in mid-April. I buy hybrid cotton seed from the county seed station, the kind in the red bag — 45 yuan per mu. Before planting, I spread one 50-kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu, the 15-15-15 kind from the dealer. That is my base. When the plants flower in early July, I top-dress with one 25-kg bag of urea per mu. The dealer told me that gives about 20 kg of nitrogen total, plus 7 or 8 kg each of phosphorus and potassium. I also spread half a cart of chicken manure per mu, which I buy from the poultry farm down the road for 80 yuan per cart.

I will irrigate four times: once right after planting to help the sprouts break through, once at flowering, once when the bolls are forming, and once in mid-August. My well has good water, but diesel for the pump is 7.5 yuan per liter now, so four times is enough. I spray pesticide five times. First spray when the seedlings are up, for aphids. Then three sprays for bollworm — I cannot skip those, the worms will eat the bolls and I will lose everything. Last spray is for red spider mites in August. Each spray costs me 14 yuan per mu for chemical.

I expect 300 jin of seed cotton per mu this year. Last year I only got 280 because July was dry. If rain is normal, 300 jin is what my land gives. My neighbor Old Zhang cut his fertilizer last year to save money and only got 220 jin per mu. He lost more than he saved. I will not make that mistake.

For stevia, I plant it in late May on the remaining 6.1 mu. I use one 40-kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base, and half a bag of urea when the plants reach 20 cm. That is about 10 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. Stevia leaves need water to stay tender, so I irrigate five times. I only spray twice for bugs — stevia does not get too many pests around here. I expect 400 jin of fresh leaves per mu, which dries down to about 200 kg. The buyer comes to the village to collect.

Seven people live in my house. Two of my sons work in Handan city and send money home, but I still pay for my granddaughter's school fees. Fertilizer and diesel are expensive this year. I will not cut back on cotton inputs — a bad cotton harvest is a disaster. For stevia, if money is tight in July, I might skip the second pesticide spray, but cotton gets everything it needs.
